providers.reason: Similar refiner tailwinds with strong YTD performance and midstream integration providing earnings stability.
providers.risk: Same margin compression risk as peers if global refining capacity normalizes.

providers.reason: Marathon Petroleum is seeing record refining margins, which doubled year-over-year to over $36 per barrel. Its high capacity utilization (94%) and aggressive shareholder returns ($2.8 billion in Q2) make it a top momentum play. Bullish analyst coverage persists as geopolitical tensions maintain high diesel and gasoline crack spreads.
providers.risk: Refinery operational outages or a sudden resolution to Middle East geopolitical tensions reducing the supply risk premium.

providers.reason: MPC shares the same record refining-crack tailwind (up ~145% YTD, diesel at $6/gallon) while its MPLX midstream stake and aggressive buybacks add stability, keeping it among S&P 500 leaders into the Sept 15 close.
providers.risk: Near-record crack spreads can normalize quickly; if fuel prices or Iran supply fears ease, MPC's stretched valuation is vulnerable to a sharp reversal.

providers.reason: Record-high refiner levered to widening crack spreads; lower valuation and higher Q2 adjusted EBITDA vs peers plus UBS Buy.
providers.risk: Overbought at all-time high; high crude input costs could squeeze margins if crack spreads narrow post-Fed.

providers.reason: High utilization targets and series of PT upgrades align with peer refining strength.
providers.risk: Same macro margin sensitivity as VLO with added execution risk on throughput goals.

providers.reason: Same record diesel and refining-margin backdrop as VLO; Q3 profits are expected well above near-record Q2 results. Mizuho lifted targets as MPC hit a 52-week high of $467.85, and heavy buybacks/dividends add support into its upcoming earnings.
providers.risk: A near-term reversal in diesel cracks from the G7 stock release or spiking crude could compress margins; the stock is extended after its 52-week-high run.
